messages:
jordyn: Uploaded a short Figma + RFC for the nav consolidation experiment. Main goals: fewer top-level items, clearer affordances for collapsed groups, and deterministic deep-link routing. PTAL: https://figma.com/file/xyz and the RFC doc in /docs/nav-rfc.md :eyes:

sanjay: skimmed the figma — love the compact grouping. Quick Q: how do we want to handle legacy permalinks? We have a bunch of external links to /console/models/:id right now.

jordyn: good point. RFC proposes canonical redirects for old paths -> new route, plus client-side fallback if the server doesn't redirect. Idea is to keep backward compatibility for existing bookmarks.

aliza: accessibility nit: when a group collapses, keyboard focus sometimes gets trapped inside the collapsed list in the prototype. We should ensure focus moves to the group button and expose aria-expanded and aria-controls. Also add a visible "skip to content" anchor at top of nav for screen readers.

matt: agree on aria props. On routing: prefer path-based deep links (e.g. /console/models/123) over hash because analytics and server-side redirects are easier. That said, hash gives us looser deploy constraints. Maybe document both strategies in the RFC and pick default.

chloe: from product perspective, recommend grouping by workflow: Models, Deployments, Observability, Billing. Users mental model is task-first, not resource-first. If we collapse 'Models' to a group, please keep 'Create model' as a prominent CTA in the group header.

jordyn: noted. We also want to avoid too many top-level nouns — thinking of a two-tier: primary groups and utility links (settings, billing).

design-bot: [accessibility-scan] Figma plugin flagged: collapsed-group chevron contrast 3.8:1 — below 4.5:1 for small icons. Suggested: increase thickness or add larger hit target.

elly: microcopy suggestion: breadcrumbs currently use "Model > Model X > Versions" — propose shortening to "Models / Model X / Versions" (slash style). Also consider truncation rules — keep root label stable to avoid width jump.

aliza: +1 to slash style for screen readers; ensure separators are aria-hidden and the active crumb uses aria-current="page".

matt: routing edge case: if we consolidate multiple subpages under a single group route, we should keep canonical query param for the view e.g. /console/models/123?tab=versions to keep permalinks stable. Example snippet: 
```
router.push(`/console/models/${id}`, { query: { tab: 'versions' } })
```
This keeps history clean and supports cross-team links.

jordyn: sweet. Actionables before next design review: 1) Sanjay + Eng to draft redirect strategy for old paths (owner: sanjay, due: Tue) 2) Aliza to write keyboard/ARIA checklist for collapse behavior (owner: aliza, due: Wed) 3) Chloe + Jordyn to finalize primary groups and CTAs in figma (owner: chloe/jordyn, due: Thu) 4) Matt to mock up server fallback + client hash fallback for staging (owner: matt, due: Fri).

chloe: can we A/B test the two breadcrumb styles for width and clarity? small cohort with telemetry on click-to-crumb rates.

jordyn: yep, add A/B test plan to RFC.

matt: one more minor: deep-link priority list in RFC should be: 1) exact path match, 2) canonical redirect mapping, 3) hash fallback, 4) server 404 -> global search fallback. That prevents users landing on broken pages.

jordyn: agreed. Thanks all — I'll update the RFC and push a new Figma iteration with the contrast fix and focus flows. :thumbsup:
